science_criteria.description: Frames the mechanistic research question and scopes the conclusion to evidence.
Performs substantive evidence analysis or reanalysis beyond a literature summary or study plan.
Analyzes inner-sphere and outer-sphere pathway evidence or explains why available evidence cannot compare them.
Examines whether electrostatic-field effects can be distinguished from direct cation coordination and correlated structural or solvation changes.

As relevant to the chosen approach, treats chemical/electronic state definitions, numerical convergence, energy/free-energy conventions, potential references, ensemble comparability, sampling, and uncertainty appropriately.
Supports positive, negative, conditional, or unresolved findings without overclaiming causality or thermodynamics.

Connects claims to traceable sources, data, methods, and evidence artifacts; independently evaluates source authenticity and the provenance of claimed calculations rather than treating hashes, logs, or self-reported convergence as proof.
Makes the analysis reproducible where applicable and explains limitations or evidence needed to discriminate mechanisms.
